Best,
Tim

# set up
library(INLA)
library(DHARMa)

# make data
dat = createData(sampleSize = 500, randomEffectVariance = 0)

# fit model
fit = inla(observedResponse ~ 1 + Environment1 , family = "poisson",
           data = dat,
           control.family=list(link='log'),
           control.predictor=list(link=1, compute=TRUE),
           control.compute=list(config = TRUE))
summary(fit)

# get and transform posterior samples
sim <- inla.posterior.sample(50, fit)
sim <- inla.posterior.sample.eval("Predictor", sim)
sim <- exp(sim) # need to exponentiate
poi <- function(x){
  x = ifelse(x<0, 0, x)
  rpois(1, x)
}
sim <- apply(sim, c(1,2), poi)

# run diagnostics
res <- createDHARMa(simulatedResponse=sim,
                    observedResponse=dat$observedResponse)
plot(res)

Once you get your sampling to work, here is some code for using DHARMa for ZIP data.

# make data for type I ZIP
n <- 100
p <- 0.8
lam <- 2
y <- rpois(n, lambda = lam)
y[rbinom(n, size=1, prob=p) == 1] = 0
dat1 <- data.frame(y=y)

# make model
mod1 <- inla(y ~ 1,
             family = "zeroinflatedpoisson1",
             data = dat1,
             control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
             control.compute=list(config=TRUE))
summary(mod1)

# get posterior samples of expectations and transforms to simulated counts
sim1 <- inla.posterior.sample(50, mod1)
sim1 <- inla.posterior.sample.eval("Predictor", sim1)
sim1 <- exp(sim1) # need exponentiation
marg1 <- mod1$marginals.hyperpar$`zero-probability parameter for zero-inflated poisson_1`
poi <- function(x, marg){
  p <- inla.rmarginal(1, marg)
  p <- 1 - p
  y <- rpois(1, x)
  y <- y * rbinom(1, size=1, prob=p)
  return(y)
}
sim1 <- apply(sim1, c(1, 2), poi, marg=marg1)

# run diagnostics in DHARMa
res <- createDHARMa(simulatedResponse=sim1,
                    observedResponse=dat1$y,
                    integerResponse = T)
plot(res)

OK, here is a way to do it with all posterior samples, rather than using inla.rmarginal().

# make data
n <- 100
p <- 0.75

lam <- 2
y <- rpois(n, lambda = lam)
y[rbinom(n, size=1, prob=p) == 1] = 0
dat1 <- data.frame(y=y)

# make model
mod1 <- inla(y ~ 1,
             family = "zeroinflatedpoisson1",
             data = dat1,
             control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
             control.compute=list(config=TRUE))
summary(mod1)

# get posterior samples of p and lambda
ss1 <- 50
samps1 <- inla.posterior.sample(ss1, mod1)
get_p <- function(...){return(theta[1])}
sim_p <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(get_p, samps1)
sim_lam <- exp(inla.posterior.sample.eval("Predictor", samps1))

# use p and lambda samples to simulate counts
out_sim <- sim_lam
for(i in 1:nrow(sim_lam)){
  for(j in 1:ncol(sim_lam)){
    p <- sim_p[,j]
p <- 1 - p

y <- rpois(1, sim_lam[i,j])
    y <- y * rbinom(n=1, size=1, prob=p)
    out_sim[i, j] <- y

}
}

# run diagnostics in DHARMa
res <- createDHARMa(simulatedResponse=out_sim,

observedResponse=dat1$y,
                    integerResponse = T)
plot(res)

I am finally getting back to this. Here is some code borrowed from the 
inlabru ZAP vignette that incorporates suggestions from Alain and Finn.
This should get you going on using DHARMa for model fit evaluation.
Note that the ZAP vignette also shows alternative ways to evaluate 
model fit using PIT histograms or Q-Q plots. 

# libraries
library(VGAM)
library(ggplot2)
library(inlabru)
library(terra) # use latest version
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# grab data and modeling objects
gorillas_sf <- inlabru::gorillas_sf
nests <- gorillas_sf$nests
mesh <- gorillas_sf$mesh
boundary <- gorillas_sf$boundary
gcov <- gorillas_sf_gcov()
counts_rstr <- terra::rasterize(vect(nests), gcov, fun = sum, background = 0) %>%
  terra::aggregate(fact = 4, fun = sum) %>% mask(vect(boundary))
counts_rstr <- counts_rstr %>% cellSize(unit = "km") %>% c(counts_rstr)

# pull counts and covariates
counts_df <- crds(counts_rstr, df = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
  bind_cols(values(counts_rstr, mat = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  rename(count = sum) %>%
  mutate(present = count > 0) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(nests))
gcov_lvls <- gcov$vegetation %>% levels()
gcov_vegetation <- gcov$vegetation %>%
  segregate() %>%
  terra::aggregate(fact = 4, fun = mean)
names(gcov_vegetation) <- gcov_lvls[[1]]$vegetation

# make mesh and spatial model
px_mesh <- fm_mesh_2d_inla(
  loc = st_intersection(st_as_sfc(counts_df), st_buffer(boundary, -0.05)),
  boundary = boundary,
  max.edge = c(0.5, 1),
  crs = st_crs(counts_df))
px_matern <- INLA::inla.spde2.pcmatern(px_mesh,
                                       prior.sigma = c(0.1, 0.01),
                                       prior.range = c(0.1, 0.01))

# define model components and likelihood
comps <- ~ veg_disturbed(gcov_vegetation$Disturbed, model = "linear") +
  veg_grassland(gcov_vegetation$Grassland, model = "linear") +
  elevation(gcov$elevation, model = "linear") +
  field(geometry, model = px_matern) + Intercept_present(1) + Intercept_count(1) +
  elevation_present(gcov$elevation, model = "linear") +
  field_present(geometry, copy = "field")
truncated_poisson_like <-
  if (package_version(getNamespaceVersion("INLA")) < "2023.10.19-1") {
    like(family = "zeroinflatedpoisson0",
      data = counts_df[counts_df$present, ],
      formula = count ~ elevation + field + Intercept_count,
      E = area,
      control.family = list(hyper = list(theta = list(
        initial = -20, fixed = TRUE))))
  } else {
    like(family = "nzpoisson",
      data = counts_df[counts_df$present, ],
      formula = count ~ elevation + field + Intercept_count,
      E = area)}

# fit zap model
fit_zap <- bru(
  comps,
  like(family = "binomial", data = counts_df,
    formula = present ~ veg_disturbed + veg_grassland +
      elevation_present + field_present + Intercept_present),
  truncated_poisson_like)
summary(fit_zap)

# get simulated count samples
pred_zap <- generate(
  fit_zap, ## this is model
  counts_df, ## these are data for prediction
  ~ {presence_prob <- ## get vector of p per posterior sample
           plogis(veg_disturbed + veg_grassland + elevation_present +
                       field_present + Intercept_present)
        lambda <- exp(elevation + field + Intercept_count) ## get lambdas
        ## simulate integer counts with function from VGAM
        sim <-  VGAM::rzapois(n=length(lambda), lambda=lambda*area,
                          pobs0=1-presence_prob)
    # define output from generate
    list(presence = presence_prob,
      lambda = lambda,
      sim = sim)},
  n.samples = 100)

# extract simulated counts from sample list object
sims <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(t(do.call(rbind,
                                   lapply(pred_zap, function(x) x[["sim"]])))))

# evaluate simulated counts with DHARMa
res <- createDHARMa(simulatedResponse=sims,
                    observedResponse=counts_df$count,
                    integerResponse = T)
plot(res)

I am finally getting back to this. Here is some code borrowed from the 
inlabru ZAP vignette that incorporates suggestions from Alain and Finn.
This should get you going on using DHARMa for model fit evaluation.
Note that the ZAP vignette also shows alternative ways to evaluate 
model fit using PIT histograms or Q-Q plots. 

# libraries
library(VGAM)
library(ggplot2)
library(inlabru)
library(terra) # use latest version
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# grab data and modeling objects
gorillas_sf <- inlabru::gorillas_sf
nests <- gorillas_sf$nests
mesh <- gorillas_sf$mesh
boundary <- gorillas_sf$boundary
gcov <- gorillas_sf_gcov()
counts_rstr <- terra::rasterize(vect(nests), gcov, fun = sum, background = 0) %>%
  terra::aggregate(fact = 4, fun = sum) %>% mask(vect(boundary))
counts_rstr <- counts_rstr %>% cellSize(unit = "km") %>% c(counts_rstr)

# pull counts and covariates
counts_df <- crds(counts_rstr, df = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
  bind_cols(values(counts_rstr, mat = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  rename(count = sum) %>%
  mutate(present = count > 0) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(nests))
gcov_lvls <- gcov$vegetation %>% levels()
gcov_vegetation <- gcov$vegetation %>%
  segregate() %>%
  terra::aggregate(fact = 4, fun = mean)
names(gcov_vegetation) <- gcov_lvls[[1]]$vegetation

# make mesh and spatial model
px_mesh <- fm_mesh_2d_inla(
  loc = st_intersection(st_as_sfc(counts_df), st_buffer(boundary, -0.05)),
  boundary = boundary,
  max.edge = c(0.5, 1),
  crs = st_crs(counts_df))
px_matern <- INLA::inla.spde2.pcmatern(px_mesh,
                                       prior.sigma = c(0.1, 0.01),
                                       prior.range = c(0.1, 0.01))

# define model components and likelihood
comps <- ~ veg_disturbed(gcov_vegetation$Disturbed, model = "linear") +
  veg_grassland(gcov_vegetation$Grassland, model = "linear") +
  elevation(gcov$elevation, model = "linear") +
  field(geometry, model = px_matern) + Intercept_present(1) + Intercept_count(1) +
  elevation_present(gcov$elevation, model = "linear") +
  field_present(geometry, copy = "field")
truncated_poisson_like <-
  if (package_version(getNamespaceVersion("INLA")) < "2023.10.19-1") {
    like(family = "zeroinflatedpoisson0",
      data = counts_df[counts_df$present, ],
      formula = count ~ elevation + field + Intercept_count,
      E = area,
      control.family = list(hyper = list(theta = list(
        initial = -20, fixed = TRUE))))
  } else {
    like(family = "nzpoisson",
      data = counts_df[counts_df$present, ],
      formula = count ~ elevation + field + Intercept_count,
      E = area)}

# fit zap model
fit_zap <- bru(
  comps,
  like(family = "binomial", data = counts_df,
    formula = present ~ veg_disturbed + veg_grassland +
      elevation_present + field_present + Intercept_present),
  truncated_poisson_like)
summary(fit_zap)

# get simulated count samples
pred_zap <- generate(
  fit_zap, ## this is model
  counts_df, ## these are data for prediction
  ~ {presence_prob <- ## get vector of p per posterior sample
           plogis(veg_disturbed + veg_grassland + elevation_present +
                       field_present + Intercept_present)
        lambda <- exp(elevation + field + Intercept_count) ## get lambdas
        ## simulate integer counts with function from VGAM
        sim <-  VGAM::rzapois(n=length(lambda), lambda=lambda*area,
                          pobs0=1-presence_prob)
    # define output from generate
    list(presence = presence_prob,
      lambda = lambda,
      sim = sim)},
  n.samples = 100)

# extract simulated counts from sample list object
sims <- as.matrix(as.data.frame(t(do.call(rbind,
                                   lapply(pred_zap, function(x) x[["sim"]])))))

# evaluate simulated counts with DHARMa
res <- createDHARMa(simulatedResponse=sims,
                    observedResponse=counts_df$count,
                    integerResponse = T)
plot(res)

OK, here is a way to do it with all posterior samples, rather than using inla.rmarginal().

# make data
n <- 100
p <- 0.75

lam <- 2
y <- rpois(n, lambda = lam)
y[rbinom(n, size=1, prob=p) == 1] = 0
dat1 <- data.frame(y=y)

# make model
mod1 <- inla(y ~ 1,
             family = "zeroinflatedpoisson1",
             data = dat1,
             control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
             control.compute=list(config=TRUE))
summary(mod1)

# get posterior samples of p and lambda
ss1 <- 50
samps1 <- inla.posterior.sample(ss1, mod1)
get_p <- function(...){return(theta[1])}
sim_p <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(get_p, samps1)
sim_lam <- exp(inla.posterior.sample.eval("Predictor", samps1))

# use p and lambda samples to simulate counts
out_sim <- sim_lam
for(i in 1:nrow(sim_lam)){
  for(j in 1:ncol(sim_lam)){
    p <- sim_p[,j]

    p <- 1 - p
    y <- rpois(1, sim_lam[i,j])
    y <- y * rbinom(n=1, size=1, prob=p)
    out_sim[i, j] <- y

  }
}

# run diagnostics in DHARMa
res <- createDHARMa(simulatedResponse=out_sim,
                    observedResponse=dat1$y,
                    integerResponse = T)
plot(res)
